$comment: LANE-EX — the EXECUTION witness for `<unistd.h>` ON pe, over the RE-EXPORT axis. ★★★ ONE SOURCE, FOUR LEGS, NO PLATFORM ARM: `main.c` contains no `#ifdef _WIN32` and no per-format spelling, so the differential is entirely in HOW the names are reached, exactly as `shipped_dirent_readdir` is a differential over the realization axis. On elf/macho every name is a symbol row in `unistd.json`; on pe that descriptor declares ZERO symbols (there is no `library.pe` key — on pe it imports nothing of its own) and instead carries two format-GATED `includes` edges, `{ header: io.h, when: { format: pe } }` and `{ header: process.h, when: { format: pe } }`, modelled on what mingw's own <unistd.h> actually is: a re-export of <io.h>/<process.h>/<getopt.h> plus a handful of locally-declared constants. ★★ THE THREE RESOLUTION PATHS ARE EXERCISED SEPARATELY, because they can fail independently: (1) `getpid` rides the process.h edge ALONE — it lives in `process.json`, no other header in this TU declares it, and no `unistd.json` arm does; (2) `open`/`close`/`read` ride the io.h edge as io.json MACROS onto `_open`/`_close`/`_read`, while `write`/`lseek`/`access`/`isatty`/`unlink`/`rmdir`/`chdir`/`getcwd` ride the SAME edge as symbol rows with a `linkName` onto the underscored ucrtbase export — two different mechanisms behind one edge, both called; (3) `SEEK_SET`/`SEEK_CUR`/`SEEK_END`, `F_OK`/`R_OK`/`W_OK` and `STD{IN,OUT,ERR}_FILENO` are declared by `unistd.json` ITSELF on pe and travel over no edge at all, so they separate 'the descriptor is available on pe' from 'the edges fire'. ★ VALUE-CORRECT, NOT MERELY LINKED: the 4 bytes are written through one fd and read back through another, the length is re-derived with lseek(SEEK_END), the post-read cursor with lseek(SEEK_CUR), and access() is checked in BOTH directions (0 on a path that exists, non-0 on one that does not, non-0 again on the same path AFTER unlink) so a stub that always answers 0 fails. Each guard has its own exit code 10..35; 42 is reachable only if every one passed. ⚠ pe SIGNATURES ARE THE MSVC/mingw ONES (`int write(int,const void*,unsigned)`, `long lseek(int,long,int)` with LLP64 32-bit long, `char *getcwd(char*,int)`), which is why every assertion compares against a small int the C conversions handle identically on both sides rather than against a width-sensitive value. ⚠ `X_OK` is DELIBERATELY NOT EXERCISED: UCRT's `_access_s` validates `(mode & ~6) == 0`, so mode 1 is EINVAL-or-invalid-parameter-handler there; the constant is a real mingw <io.h> value and ships, but calling it would make this a Windows-crash test. `isatty` is called on a VALID fd (an invalid one trips UCRT's invalid-parameter handler -> `__fastfail` -> 0xC0000409, silent, and reads exactly like a struct-shape miscompile) and asserted `== 0`, never `== 1` (MSVC documents a NONZERO return for a character device). ★ THE STDOUT PIN CARRIES NO NEWLINE ON PURPOSE — fd 1 is TEXT-mode on pe, so a '\n' would arrive as CRLF on Windows and LF elsewhere and force a per-target `expectedStdout` override, i.e. the manifest would stop asserting that the four legs AGREE, which is the entire point of a one-source example. ★★ RED-ON-DISABLE — FOUR MUTATIONS, EACH ACTUALLY RUN (2026-08-18) against a COPY of the config tree under `DSS_CONFIG_ROOT` (a repo-root-shaped dir containing `src/dss-config/`), never against the repo; every mutant was checked to differ byte-wise, to still parse as JSON, and to no longer contain the witness text, and an UNMUTATED control was re-measured before and after each one (rc=0 both times, so the restored bytes are proven to have reached the process). (a) DROP `pe` FROM `unistd.json`'s `availableObjectFormats` -> rc=1 on pe64 debug AND release: `error[C_UnbackedPredefinedMacro] predefined macro '__MINGW32__' … requires shipped header 'unistd.h' on object format 'pe', but that header's descriptor declares it does NOT exist on 'pe'` (and the `__MINGW64__` twin, and `error[D_SchemaLoadFailed]` for the shipped runtime unit `runtime/platform/src/dirent.c`, which fails for the same reason). (b) REWRITE the io.h edge in the UNCONDITIONAL (bare-string) form `"io.h",` so it fires on every format -> pe64 stays green (io.h IS available there) and elf64 + macho64 go rc=1 with `error[F001D]: io.h` pointed at this file's `#include <unistd.h>` line: EDGE FIRES => CHILD AVAILABLE, enforced. ⓘ Spelling that same edge as an OBJECT with the `when` deleted (`{ "header": "io.h" }`) is a different thing — a malformed entry, refused with `error[F_ShippedLibDescriptorMalformed] … includes[0]: a conditional 'includes' entry requires a 'when' object …; an UNCONDITIONAL edge is spelled as a bare header-name string` — and it takes the WHOLE descriptor down, S0001-ing every name in this file on every format. (c) DELETE the `process.h` edge -> pe64 rc=1 with exactly `error[S0001]: [target=x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec] getpid` while elf64 stays rc=0: the sharpest of the four, because it reds THIS example and nothing else about it. (d) DELETE io.json's `isatty` symbol row (edges intact, and no predefined-macro surface claim names it, so nothing masks the source-level verdict) -> pe64 rc=1 on BOTH arms with `error[S0001]: … isatty`, elf64 rc=0. ⚠ MEASURED AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU RUN (a) OR (c): the predefined-macro surface-claim block on `__MINGW32__`/`__MINGW64__` in `c-subset.lang.json` (spelled `requires` when this was measured) names `getpid`/`close`/`read`, so it fires FIRST and its `C_UnbackedPredefinedMacro` is what you see; the source-level `S0001` only surfaces once that claim is narrowed. That guard is a feature — it makes the identity macro a checked consequence of the realized surface — but it means a reader of the recipe must not expect an include-site diagnostic. RUN LEGS (2026-08-18, this host): pe64-x86_64 debug + release rc=42 stdout `unistd-reexport-ok`; elf64-x86_64 under WSL and elf64-aarch64 under qemu-aarch64 (QEMU_LD_PREFIX=/usr/aarch64-linux-gnu), debug + release, all rc=42 with identical stdout; macho64-arm64 COMPILES clean here (debug + release) and executes on the `macos-latest` Apple-Silicon leg, the `shipped_dirent_readdir` convention. The `release` arm is mandatory and load-bearing here: this example's whole body is calls whose results feed the exit ladder, which is precisely the shape DCE and CSE get to reason about.
